newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NO SPECIFIC PLANS FOR UNIT SALE GAIN-UCB.
newsitem.headline: NO SPECIFIC PLANS FOR UNIT SALE GAIN-UCB.

text.p: Belgian drugs and chemicals group UCB said on Wednesday it would use the capital gain from the sale of its fine chemicals unit to boost its treasury position, adding that for now it had no specific plans for the cash.
"We will use the money to strengthen our treasury, but we have no specific plans," a UCB spokesman said.

UCB said on Tuesday it had sold its UCB Fine Chemicals subsidiary to Belgium's Proviron NV for undisclosed terms, adding it expected to book a capital gain of around 400 million Belgian francs on the transaction.
The spokesman said the deal marked the end of a review of UCB's position in the chemicals sector.
It is the company's declared strategy to be among the world leaders in the market segments in which it operates.
This was not the case as regards fine chemicals, the spokesman said, "it is not a core business." UCB would have had to pump further cash into the unit to strengthen its international position.
The four business units now left in UCB's Chemical Sector are resins and specialty chemicals, polyester powders, methylamines and derivatives, and polyurethane and acrylic resins.
